senses.tr: ilk çıkış, ilk gösteri, ilk maç
senses.def: the first public appearance of a performer, player, or product
examples: She made her Broadway debut at the age of nineteen.
The band's debut album sold a million copies.

senses.tr: ilk kez sahneye çıkmak, ilk kez piyasaya sürülmek
senses.def: to appear or be shown to the public for the first time
examples: The new phone debuts in stores next month.

note: French origin: the t is silent. Often used as an adjective: debut album, debut season.

senses.def: a period of ten years
examples: Prices have doubled over the past decade.
The 1960s were a decade of huge social change.

note: "Decades" is often used to mean "a very long time": "for decades".

senses.def: the twelfth and last month of the year
examples: The store gets very busy in December before the holidays.
My birthday is on December 3.

note: Always capitalized. Use "in December" for the month and "on December 3" for a date.

senses.tr: makul, düzgün, fena değil, tatmin edici
senses.def: of a good enough standard or quality
examples: It's hard to find a decent apartment for less than $2,000 a month.
Everyone deserves a decent wage.

senses.def: honest, fair, and kind, following accepted moral standards
examples: He's a decent guy who would never cheat anyone.
Do the decent thing and apologize.

senses.def: wearing enough clothes not to be embarrassed
examples: Can I come in? Are you decent?

note: Pronounced /ˈdiːsnt/. Don't confuse with "descent" /dɪˈsent/ (going down).

senses.def: to choose what to do after thinking about the possibilities
examples: We decided to sell the house and move to Denver.
I can't decide which dress to wear.

senses.def: to affect the result of something
examples: A single goal decided the championship.

note: "Decide on" = choose: "We decided on the blue sofa." "Decide against" = choose not to.

senses.def: a choice you make after thinking about what is best to do
examples: Moving abroad was the best decision I ever made.
The judge's decision will be announced tomorrow.

note: In American English you "make" a decision; "take a decision" is British.

senses.def: the process of making important decisions, especially in an organization
examples: Employees want to be more involved in decision-making.
Stress can seriously affect your decision-making.

senses.def: very important in deciding the final result
examples: Her testimony was decisive in winning the case.
The army won a decisive victory.

senses.def: able to make decisions quickly and with confidence
examples: A good leader needs to be decisive in a crisis.

senses.def: the outside floor of a ship, or one of the floors of a ship or bus
examples: The passengers went up on deck to watch the sunset.
We sat on the top deck of the tour bus.

senses.def: a wooden floor built outside a house, usually raised above the ground
examples: We had dinner out on the back deck.

senses.def: a complete set of playing cards
examples: Shuffle the deck and deal five cards to each player.

note: "All hands on deck" = everyone must help. Americans say "a deck of cards"; British say "a pack".

senses.def: an official or formal statement, or the act of making one
examples: The Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776.
The president made a declaration of war.

senses.def: a written statement giving official information, such as income or goods
examples: Fill out the customs declaration before you land.

senses.def: to say something officially or publicly
examples: The governor declared a state of emergency after the floods.
The company was declared bankrupt in 2019.

senses.def: to tell officials about money you earned or goods you are bringing into a country
examples: Do you have anything to declare?

senses.def: to say something clearly and firmly
examples: "I'm never going back there," she declared.

senses.def: a gradual decrease in number, value, quality, or strength
examples: There has been a sharp decline in birth rates.
The town went into decline when the factory closed.

senses.def: to become smaller, fewer, or worse
examples: Sales declined by 15% last quarter.
His health declined rapidly after the fall.

senses.def: to politely refuse an offer or invitation
examples: She declined the job offer.
The senator declined to comment.

note: "Your card was declined" = the payment was refused.

senses.def: to make something look more attractive by adding things to it
examples: We decorated the tree with lights and ornaments.
The cake was decorated with fresh strawberries.

senses.def: to paint or put wallpaper and furniture in a room or house
examples: They decorated the baby's room in soft yellow.

senses.def: to give someone a medal or honor
examples: He was decorated for bravery during the war.

senses.def: something added to make a place or thing look attractive, especially for a special occasion
examples: We put up the Christmas decorations in early December.
The walls were bare, with no decoration at all.

senses.def: the way a room or building is painted and furnished
examples: The hotel's interior decoration is very modern.

senses.def: a medal given as an honor
examples: He received several military decorations.

senses.def: a reduction in size, number, or amount
examples: There was a 10% decrease in crime last year.
Doctors noticed a decrease in her blood pressure.

senses.def: to become smaller or fewer, or to make something smaller
examples: The number of smokers has decreased steadily since the 1990s.
The new road should decrease traffic downtown.

note: Stress moves: the noun is /ˈdiːkriːs/, the verb usually /dɪˈkriːs/. Opposite: increase.

senses.def: working hard at something because it is very important to you
examples: She's a dedicated teacher who stays late to help her students.
The charity is run by a small team of dedicated volunteers.

senses.def: made or used for only one particular purpose
examples: The building has a dedicated bike lane and charging stations.

senses.def: hard work and effort that someone gives to something they think is important
examples: Her dedication to her patients is remarkable.
It takes years of dedication to become a concert pianist.

senses.def: words at the start of a book or song that say who it is written for
examples: The dedication at the front of the book reads, "For my mother."

senses.def: to reach a conclusion by thinking about the facts or evidence you have
examples: From the mud on his boots, she deduced that he had been in the garden.
Scientists deduced the age of the rock from its chemical makeup.

note: Formal. Don't confuse with "deduct" (to take away an amount, e.g. from pay); both share the noun "deduction".

senses.def: something someone does, especially something very good or very bad
examples: Helping the old man carry his groceries was her good deed for the day.
He was punished for his evil deeds.

senses.def: a legal document showing who owns a house or land
examples: Keep the deed to the house in a safe place.

note: Formal or literary in the "action" sense, except in the common phrase "good deed".

senses.tr: saymak, addetmek, kabul etmek, uygun görmek
senses.def: to consider or judge someone or something in a particular way
examples: The building was deemed unsafe after the earthquake.
Officials will take whatever action they deem necessary.

note: Formal; often passive: "was deemed safe". No "as": "deemed it necessary", not "deemed it as necessary".

senses.def: going a long way down from the top or surface, or a long way in
examples: The lake is very deep in the middle.
He has a deep cut on his leg.

senses.def: very strong or serious, or (of sounds) low
examples: She fell into a deep sleep.
He has a deep voice that's perfect for radio.

senses.def: (of colors) dark and strong
examples: The walls were painted a deep red.

senses.def: a long way below the surface or far inside something
examples: The miners worked deep underground.
They walked deep into the forest.

note: "Deep down" = in your true feelings: "Deep down, he knew she was right."

senses.def: very much or very strongly
examples: I'm deeply sorry for your loss.
The community was deeply divided over the new law.

senses.def: a long way down or in
examples: Breathe deeply and try to relax.

note: Use "deeply" for feelings (deeply moved); use "deep" for physical distance (dig deep).

senses.def: what happens or is used automatically if you do not choose something else, especially on a computer
examples: The default language is English, but you can change it in Settings.
Restore the phone to its default settings.

senses.def: failure to pay back a loan or debt
examples: The country is close to default on its foreign debt.

senses.def: to fail to pay money that you owe
examples: Thousands of homeowners defaulted on their mortgages in 2008.

note: "By default" also means "because nobody else did": "She won by default when the other player didn't show up."

senses.def: failure to win a game, war, or election
examples: It was the team's worst defeat in twenty years.
The party suffered a heavy defeat in the election.

senses.def: to win against someone in a war, game, or competition
examples: Spain defeated Germany 2–1 in the final.
The rebels were finally defeated after a long war.

senses.def: to stop something from succeeding, or to vote against it
examples: The bill was defeated in the Senate by three votes.

note: "Defeat the purpose" = make something pointless.

senses.def: a fault in something or in the way it was made
examples: The cars were recalled because of a defect in the brakes.
She was born with a heart defect.

senses.def: to leave your country, party, or group to join an opposing one
examples: The spy defected to the West in 1985.

note: Noun stress: /ˈdiːfekt/; verb stress: /dɪˈfekt/.

senses.def: to protect someone or something from attack or harm
examples: The soldiers defended the city for three months.
She took classes to learn how to defend herself.

senses.def: to speak or write in support of someone or something that is criticized
examples: The minister defended the decision to raise taxes.

senses.def: to act as someone's lawyer in court, or to try to keep a title in a competition
examples: A well-known lawyer will defend him at the trial.
She is defending her Olympic title this year.

senses.def: a player whose main job is to stop the other team from scoring
examples: The defender cleared the ball just before it crossed the line.
They signed a young central defender from Brazil.

senses.def: a person who protects someone or something or speaks in support of them
examples: She's a passionate defender of free speech.

note: In the US, a "public defender" is a lawyer paid by the state to defend people who can't afford one.

senses.def: the act of protecting someone or something from attack or criticism
examples: The country spends billions on defense every year.
He spoke in defense of his colleague.

senses.def: the arguments and lawyers that try to show in court that someone is not guilty
examples: The defense argued that the evidence was unreliable.

senses.def: the players in a team whose job is to stop the other side from scoring
examples: Our defense has been weak all season.

note: American spelling; British is "defence". In US sports it is often stressed /ˈdiːfens/.

senses.def: used or intended to protect against attack
examples: Troops built defensive positions along the river.
The coach changed to a more defensive strategy.

senses.def: reacting as if you are being criticized, even when you are not
examples: He gets very defensive whenever I mention his drinking.

note: "On the defensive" = having to defend yourself against attack or criticism.

senses.def: a lack of something that is needed, especially in the body
examples: Vitamin D deficiency is common in people who don't get much sun.
Iron deficiency can make you feel tired.

senses.def: a weakness or fault in something
examples: The report pointed out serious deficiencies in the safety system.

senses.def: the amount by which money spent is greater than money received
examples: The government is trying to reduce the budget deficit.
The country has run a trade deficit for decades.

senses.def: the amount by which a team is behind, or a lack of something
examples: The team came back from a 15-point deficit to win.
Some children with attention deficits need extra support.

note: Opposite: surplus. "Deficit" is about money or scores; "deficiency" is usually about the body or quality.

senses.def: to explain the meaning of a word or idea
examples: How would you define "success"?
The law defines a child as anyone under 18.

senses.def: to describe or show something clearly, or to be a key feature of something
examples: The contract clearly defines each person's responsibilities.
That one moment defined his entire career.

note: "A defining moment" = a moment that shows or decides the true nature of someone or something.

senses.def: certain and not likely to change
examples: We don't have a definite date for the wedding yet.
Is that a definite yes?

senses.def: easy to see or notice; clear
examples: There's been a definite improvement in her grades.

note: Common spelling mistake: "definate". "Definite" = certain; "definitive" = final and most authoritative.

senses.def: used to emphasize that something is true and there is no doubt
examples: I'll definitely be there on Saturday.
This is definitely the best pizza in town.

note: Often used alone as a strong "yes": "Are you coming?" "Definitely!"

senses.def: a statement explaining what a word or idea means
examples: Look up the definition in a dictionary.
There's no single definition of happiness.

senses.def: how clear an image or sound is
examples: The new TV has amazing picture definition.

note: "By definition" = because of what something is: "A circle is, by definition, round."

senses.tr: karşı gelmek, hiçe saymak, meydan okumak
senses.def: to refuse to obey a person, law, or rule
examples: Thousands defied the ban and marched through the city.
He defied his parents and dropped out of college.

senses.def: to be impossible to explain, describe, or believe
examples: The beauty of the canyon defies description.
The plane's flight seemed to defy gravity.

note: "Defy the odds" = succeed although it seemed very unlikely.

senses.def: a unit for measuring temperature or angles
examples: It's 90 degrees outside, so wear sunscreen.
A right angle is 90 degrees.

senses.def: an amount or level of something
examples: The job requires a high degree of skill.
To some degree, I agree with you.

senses.def: a qualification given by a university after completing a course
examples: She has a degree in computer science from Stanford.

note: US temperatures are usually in Fahrenheit: 90°F is about 32°C.

senses.def: a period when someone or something has to wait or is late
examples: Bad weather caused long delays at the airport.
Please reply without delay.

senses.def: to make someone or something late, or to do something later than planned
examples: Our flight was delayed by three hours.
They decided to delay the wedding until next spring.

senses.def: a person chosen to represent a group, especially at a meeting or conference
examples: Delegates from 50 countries attended the climate summit.
Each state sends delegates to the party convention.

senses.def: to give part of your work or authority to someone else
examples: A good manager knows how to delegate tasks to the team.

note: Noun ends /ɡət/; verb ends /ɡeɪt/.

senses.def: a group of people sent to represent a country or organization
examples: A trade delegation from China arrived in Washington on Monday.
The delegation met with the prime minister.

senses.def: the act of giving part of your work or authority to someone else
examples: Effective delegation saves managers a lot of time.

senses.def: to remove something written, printed, or stored on a computer
examples: I accidentally deleted all my photos.
She deleted the post after people complained.

senses.def: done on purpose, not by accident
examples: Police believe the fire was a deliberate act.
It was a deliberate attempt to mislead the public.

senses.def: slow and careful
examples: He walked to the stage with slow, deliberate steps.

senses.def: to think about or discuss something carefully before deciding
examples: The jury deliberated for two days before reaching a verdict.

note: Adjective ends /ət/; verb ends /eɪt/. Opposite of the adjective: accidental.

senses.def: on purpose, not by accident
examples: He deliberately ignored my messages.
The fire was started deliberately.

senses.def: slowly and carefully
examples: She spoke slowly and deliberately so everyone could understand.

senses.def: easily damaged or broken
examples: Wash delicate fabrics by hand.
The vase is very delicate, so be careful.

senses.def: needing to be handled carefully to avoid upsetting people
examples: Money can be a delicate subject between friends.
The negotiations are at a delicate stage.

senses.def: small and beautiful, or (of taste or color) light and pleasant
examples: The fish has a delicate flavor that goes well with lemon.

note: "Delicacy" also means an expensive or special food: "Caviar is a delicacy."

senses.def: having a very pleasant taste or smell
examples: Thanks for dinner; the soup was delicious.
A delicious smell of fresh bread came from the kitchen.

note: "Delicious" is already strong, so say "absolutely delicious", not "very delicious".

senses.def: a feeling of great pleasure, or something that gives great pleasure
examples: The children screamed with delight when they saw the snow.
Her garden is an absolute delight.

senses.def: to give someone great pleasure
examples: The magic show delighted kids and adults alike.

senses.def: to enjoy something very much, especially something others might not like
examples: He delights in proving people wrong.

senses.def: very pleased and happy
examples: We're delighted to announce the birth of our daughter.
She was delighted with her exam results.

note: "I'd be delighted" is a polite way to accept an invitation.

senses.def: to take goods, letters, or packages to a person or place
examples: The package will be delivered on Friday.
Do you deliver pizza to this neighborhood?

senses.def: to do what you promised or what is expected
examples: The new phone fails to deliver on its promises.
If you want the job, you have to deliver results.

senses.def: to give a speech or talk, or to help a baby be born
examples: The president delivered a speech on the economy.
The midwife delivered three babies last night.

senses.def: the act of taking goods or letters to the people they were sent to
examples: The store offers free delivery on orders over $50.
We're expecting a delivery this afternoon.

senses.def: the process of giving birth to a baby
examples: The delivery went smoothly, and both mother and baby are healthy.

senses.def: the way someone speaks in public
examples: His ideas were good, but his delivery was dull.

senses.def: a very firm request for something
examples: The workers' main demand is a 10% pay raise.
The kidnappers made demands for money.

senses.def: the need or wish of people to have or buy something
examples: Demand for electric cars is growing fast.
Nurses are in high demand right now.

senses.def: to ask for something very firmly, as if you have a right to it
examples: The customer demanded a full refund.
Protesters demanded that the mayor resign.

senses.def: to need something such as time, skill, or effort
examples: This job demands a lot of patience.

note: No "for" after the verb: "demand an answer", not "demand for an answer". The noun takes "for": "demand for housing".
